note: Stateless Language Agents (arXiv 2610.07625v1, 6 Oct 2026). Data numbers on screen: 1B (a token budget, not a result), 98% (one CORAL baseline run on a GPU kernel task), 84% (fewer tokens to first match the strongest baseline's full-budget result, Anthropic kernel task, Claude Code setup, one run per method; the lower of the two setups) and <0.6% (the Advisor's share of tokens, not of cost, in two analyzed runs). All results are the authors' own runs. The close answers the hook only for the kernel task and the four FrontierSWE tasks (final results beat the quarter-budget results, Tables 1 and 2), with a chip for the SOL-ExecBench task where no method moved much. Every other digit on screen is the arXiv id, an axis origin, or a source tag (section, table, figure, appendix, page).

numbers.1: 1B tokens, the x-axis end of the l02 sketch and of the l11 bars: a token budget, not a result. Figure 2(b) caption (p. 3): in the CORAL run 'token consumption continues to 1B'. The Anthropic kernel task budget is 1B (Table 1, p. 8: '100% (1B)'). Also page 1 and sec 1 in source tags.
numbers.98: 98% of the final 1,500 sessions make no tool calls while token consumption continues, in one CORAL run on a GPU kernel task (sec 1, p. 2; Figure 2(b), p. 3: '79 calls; 98% no tools'). A baseline run by the authors, not SLA. The l02 chip says 'one baseline run · GPU kernel task'.
numbers.84: Over 84% fewer cumulative tokens for SLA to first match the strongest baseline's full-budget result on the Anthropic kernel task (Abstract, p. 1: 'over 84% fewer tokens'; Table 1, p. 8: Claude Code, one run per method, SLA 138.5M vs CORAL 888.3M, -84.4%). The lower of the two coding-agent setups; with Codex (mean curve of three runs, vs SwarmResearch) the reduction is 93.1% (67.9M vs 986.3M). Tokens, not cost. On screen with chips 'Anthropic kernel task', 'Claude Code setup · one run', 'lower of two setups'.
numbers.0.6: The Advisor consumes less than 0.6% of tokens (Abstract, p. 1; sec 4.4 and Table 5, p. 10): 0.24% (Anthropic kernel, 1B tokens) and 0.51% (FrontierSWE libexpat, 700M tokens), the two analyzed runs. Its share of estimated model cost is higher, 1.20% and 2.29%, because it reuses less cache (sec 4.4, p. 9 to 10). On screen with 'share of tokens' and 'not cost: its cost share is higher'.

claims.l01: A question, not a claim. 'Budgets of up to one billion tokens' (Abstract, p. 1); the paper's central question (sec 1, p. 2): 'how can automated research sustain progress as its inference budget grows?'
claims.l02: 'more inference does not by itself produce more progress' (Abstract). 'In one CORAL run on a GPU kernel task, the last improvement arrives at 231M tokens' and token consumption continues to 1B (sec 1, p. 2; Figure 2(b), p. 3). The step curve is a sketch of Figure 2(b), labelled as a sketch on screen.
claims.l03: '98% of the final 1,500 sessions make no tool calls while token consumption continues' (sec 1, p. 2). Same baseline run; the chip from l02 stays up.
claims.l04: 'We trace these failures to two choices: where research state lives and who decides what to try next' (Abstract). The three failure labels quote the Abstract: 'agents replay growing histories, duplicate one another's work, or stop experimenting'.
claims.l05: CORAL: 'Each CORAL agent keeps one long-running session, which CORAL resumes after every heartbeat, stall, or restart'. SwarmResearch: 'The Shepherd runs as a long-running session, and each Optimizer starts by resuming its parent agent's conversation' (sec 4.1, p. 6 to 7). EvoX, the third baseline, starts a fresh coding agent per generation, so the line says 'two baselines'.
claims.l06: Abstract (p. 1): 'no agent carries its conversation across invocations; instead, the harness owns the research state (candidate solutions and measured outcomes)'. Spoken as 'agents keep no conversation between calls. The code and the scores carry over' (calls = invocations; code and scores = candidate solutions and measured outcomes). The receipt shows the paper's own words, cropped to 'no agent carries its conversation ... across invocations'. On screen 'SLA: the new method' names the method; the board plate says 'kept between calls'.
claims.l07: 'reconstructs a fresh and role-specific context for every invocation' (Abstract). Advisor context: task, global best code and score, evidence summary across search directions (sec 3.1). Worker context: task, its assignment, its retained candidate, compact local feedback (sec 3.1). 'Workers build on prior progress without inheriting the conversations that produced it' (sec 3.1, p. 5). The robot dropping its tray of chat bubbles is a picture of 'loses the conversation'; the board keeping candidates and scores is 'not the work'.
claims.l08: 'a stateless Advisor reads harness-summarized evidence across search directions and assigns concrete experiments to parallel Workers' (Abstract); 'parallel Workers run distinct experiments instead of repeating each other's work' (sec 1).
claims.l09: Appendix D.3 and Figure 5(a) (p. 21 to 22): in the first libexpat ablation run without Advisor assignments, all three Workers add the same XML entity-decoding code from the same starting code (trials 269 to 271) and none improves the starting score. The paper notes similar overlap in both other runs and that trace examples 'do not measure how often these behaviors occur'. The line says 'in one run' and the chip says 'a trace example, not a rate'.
claims.l10: Table 5 and sec 4.4: Advisor 0.24% and 0.51% of tokens; 1.20% and 2.29% of estimated cost. The line says 'tokens'; the chip says its cost share is higher.
claims.l11: Table 1 (p. 8), Claude Code setup, one run per method: CORAL reaches its full-budget result (1130 cycles) at 888.3M tokens; SLA (spoken 'the method') first matches it at 138.5M (-84.4%). Abstract: 'reaches the strongest kernel baseline's final performance with over 84% fewer tokens'. Bars drawn from the two token counts on a 1B axis.
claims.l12: Sec 4.2 and Table 2 (p. 7 to 8), FrontierSWE, Codex, one run per method: 'SLA trails the strongest baseline on all four tasks at 25% of the budget but leads on all four at the full budget'. 'Then it improved more': SLA's own score rose from 175M to 700M on all four tasks (18.82 to 31.33, 20.42 to 28.84, 15.43 to 45.27, 80.22 to 96.15), and by more than the strongest baseline's (Table 2 deltas -0.85/-3.90/-11.27/-2.75 at 175M become +6.75/+0.86/+6.68/+5.49 at 700M).
claims.l13: Sec 5, Limitations (p. 11): 'All tasks have executable evaluators, so goals that are vague or slow to evaluate remain untested' (spoken as 'Every task had an automatic score'; the fog card says 'vague or slow goals' and 'untested'). 'Our ablations change what each agent sees, not whether it keeps its conversation across invocations' (spoken as 'No test let these agents keep their conversations'). 'most configurations use a single run' (chip).
claims.l14: Answer to the hook, scoped to what the paper reports. Best-so-far results at 25% vs 100% of the budget for SLA: Anthropic kernel task, Table 1 (p. 8): Codex 1149.3 cycles at 250M vs 1112.0 at 1B (mean of three runs), Claude Code 1079 vs 1039 (one run), lower is better; FrontierSWE, Table 2 (p. 8): all four scores higher at 700M than at 175M (one Codex run each). Figure 1 caption: 'SLA sustains research progress over long horizons.' Not every task: on SOL-ExecBench #210 'no method, including SLA, improves by more than 0.02 between 25% and 100% of the budget' (sec 4.2, p. 7), shown as the chip 'on one SOL-ExecBench task, no method moved much' (no number printed; SLA's own final result still beat its quarter-budget result there, 0.377 to 0.393, Table 3). Close advice: sec 1 (p. 3) 'We therefore report results at multiple cumulative token budgets and encourage future evaluations to do the same' (tag: 'the paper's advice: report several budgets').
